clue.text: Present leg

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small Christmas gift tucked into a hung-up sock
second meaning, taken literally: a limb is what occupies a sock or tight

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it looks like a command or a description of a limb; the second meaning is a playful literal reading of the phrase, since a leg is what fills hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Christmas gifts placed in a hanging sock are called by this name, and a leg literally occupies hosiery.

clue.text: 'Man or Dogs' passage read out

definitions.note: the Isle of Man and the Isle of Dogs; the answer is what both are

indicators.note: reading something out means saying it, so we want a word that is spoken the same as another

parts.note: a passage between rows of seats is an aisle, which is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: A quoted title, 'Man or Dogs', has a passage read aloud from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Man and Dogs look like a book title; they are two places, the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea and the Isle of Dogs in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Isle of Man and the Isle of Dogs carry this word as part of their official place names.

clue.text: Serving idiot regularly upset ballot

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something tips it over so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a ballot is a poll, a vote

explanation.surface: A person in service is an idiot who keeps upsetting the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' looks like a participle describing the idiot, but it is a noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless spoonful of food, so it is a serving or helping on a plate.

clue.text: Appreciated little protection for Malcolm, orphaned and left out

indicators.note: protecting something means wrapping around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for small

indicators.note: something out is absent or excluded, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: the name taken as written, before anything is removed
an orphan has lost mother, so these letters go from the name
L is the standard abbreviation for left; one is removed

explanation.surface: A boy called Malcolm, orphaned and excluded, appreciates the little protection he is given.
explanation.walkthrough: An orphan has lost mother, so the name drops its MA; L is the standard abbreviation for left. Wee is Scottish and informal British for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome is gladly received, so it is appreciated by the person who gets it.

clue.text: Change tramline's last stop

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to alter the final stop on a tram route.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive, but it stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition; 'last' belongs with 'stop', not with tramline.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the station at the end of a bus, train or tram route, where services finish.

clue.text: American celebrity into abusing cocaine briefly

indicators.note: being brief means cutting short, so the word loses its final letter
going into something means sitting inside it
abusing something is mistreating it, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the drug without its last letter
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A US celebrity is into abusing cocaine for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' looks like it means someone from the US, but Central Americans count too; STAR goes into a jumble of COCAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica lies in Central America, so a person from there is an American in the continental sense.

clue.text: As a rule, a biro or otherwise can show a spectacular vision

indicators.note: 'otherwise' means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.words: As a rule, a biro or
parts.note: every letter of these words, taken together

explanation.surface: Generally, a ballpoint pen or some other instrument can draw something spectacular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' looks like a phrase meaning generally, but its letters are fodder; the comma is there only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are shimmering curtains of colour in the polar night sky, a famously spectacular sight.

clue.text: Device that examines and controls croupier's odds

indicators.note: odds and evens: take alternate letters rather than whole words

parts.note: the even-placed letters of this word
the odd-placed letters of this word

explanation.surface: A gadget that checks and controls the odds a casino croupier offers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gambling; alternate letters run through both words, starting on the second letter of the first and the first letter of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor uses this instrument to look into the ear canal and eardrum, so it is a device for examination.

clue.text: Leaving the Guardian to follow old backwards party

indicators.note: following means coming after, which fixes the order of the parts

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: going backwards means reading from right to left

parts.note: a do is an informal party
the newspaper speaking of itself: we, us

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the Guardian to work for an old-fashioned, backward-looking party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the paper this puzzle appears in, so it refers to itself as US; 'the Guardian' and 'party' look political but are just letter sources.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure of people, so it is a leaving on a large scale.

clue.text: Top came off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or not right, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lid or garment came loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a lid coming off; 'Top' is a noun meaning the highest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of achievement, so it is the top.

clue.text: Moving crazy shit

parts.note: loco is slang for mad
a bowel motion is a polite term for excrement

explanation.surface: Shifting some absurd rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like an adjective (touching), but it is the act of going from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the power or act of travelling from one place to another, so it is moving as a noun.

clue.text: Snag this Latin prize

parts.note: hic is Latin for this
a trophy cup is a prize

explanation.surface: Win this prize in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snag' reads as a verb (grab the prize), but it is a noun: a small setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor difficulty or temporary setback, so it is a snag in a plan.

clue.text: Wine and champagne to start erection? No!

indicators.note: a start is a beginning, so take only the opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter
slang for a stiffened penis
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Wine and champagne to kick things off, and no erection: a familiar drunken disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ribald surface hides a plain charade; 'and' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white grape variety and the dry white table drink made from it.

clue.text: My French later turned out to be useful here

definitions.text: My French later turned out to be useful here

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: something turned out has been turned inside out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that their schoolroom French came in handy after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the city is in French-speaking Quebec, so French is useful there, while the first four words also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Montreal is mostly francophone, so a visitor's French would prove valuable in it.

clue.text: Native Americans sent back soldier to get sauna treatment …

definitions.note: lizards native to the Americas, not people

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, right to left

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: treating something works it over, so its letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Native people send a returning soldier for a sweat-lodge style sauna treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Americans' wants to mean people; these natives are reptiles. The ellipsis carries on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large lizards whose home range is Central and South America, so they are animals native there.

clue.text: Perhaps true lady is being untrue

indicators.note: 'perhaps' signals one possible version among others, so the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A supposedly faithful woman turns out to be cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sets 'true' against 'untrue', a neat irony; the definition is the act, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual unfaithfulness to a spouse, and being unfaithful in that way is being untrue.

clue.text: … one that doesn't cure hygiene problem on set

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it

parts.note: to set something down is to place it
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Continuing from the sauna: the treatment does nothing for a body odour problem on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a film set, but it is a verb meaning put; the ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue only.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug, so it is a treatment that does not actually heal anything.

clue.text: See 7
Politician marking time? Changing leaders would be smarter

parts.note: these two words only supply their initials, M and T, to say which letters trade places

indicators.note: changing things over means swapping their places, so two letters exchange positions
leaders are the front runners, so it is the first letters of the nearby words that are swapped

parts.note: taken as written; its M and T trade places

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician doing nothing much: replacing the party leader would be the smarter move.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Labour leader; 'marking time' hints at swapping the M and the T, the leading letters of 'marking' and 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer is a British Labour politician who became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in 2024.

clue.text: See 22 Down
See 1
Sway in to find guard

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word; its remaining three letters are read with the next word
an entry is a way in

explanation.surface: Using influence to get a guard posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sway' looks like one word meaning influence; split it as S plus 'way', and 'way in' becomes the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch at a gate or camp, so it is a guard.

clue.text: How to fob us off about a couple of advertisements causing little suspicion

indicators.note: something off and about is out of place and all over, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
two ads, AD twice

explanation.surface: A guide to dismissing customers with a few adverts, which provokes slight mistrust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to' looks like a guide's title, but those two words are fodder too; all fourteen letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a shadow of a doubt' means the smallest trace of uncertainty, so it is a little suspicion.

clue.text: Sky shows song by Mercury?

parts.note: Mercury is one example, hence the question mark
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A song by Freddie Mercury of Queen, the sort that features in big sky-themed shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury wants to be Freddie Mercury the singer, especially next to 'song'; here it is the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are domed theatres that project images of stars and planets onto the ceiling for audiences.

clue.text: Hogwash in barrel, although emptied twice

indicators.note: emptying something removes its contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
the two shells already joined, written out a second time

explanation.surface: Pig swill in a barrel that has been emptied twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogwash looks like literal pig food to go with the barrel; it means nonsense. Both shells are joined and then the whole thing is repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash means nonsense, and the repeated phrase is used for tedious, meaningless talk.

clue.text: See 24 Across
Fix couple one more time

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Arrange for a couple to get together once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 're-pair', the answer means couple again, which is exactly what the wordplay says.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it so it works again, which is to fix it.

clue.text: Say Arab has a sense of self-importance

parts.note: e.g., for example
someone from Oman is one kind of Arab
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab man is said to be rather full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for instance' introducing the whole idea; it supplies EG, with OMANI as the example Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself, an inflated feeling of personal importance.
